newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: New woes for S.Africa's Winnie Madikizela-Mandela.
newsitem.headline: New woes for S.Africa's Winnie Madikizela-Mandela.

text.p: South Africa's outspoken women's leader Winnie Madikizela-Mandela on Wednesday blamed covert intelligence forces for tampering with her luggage at Brussels Airport.

Madikizela-Mandela, the former wife of President Nelson Mandela who swept to victory at the helm of the ruling party's women's league last weekend, flew into Belgium to attend a May Day rally and workers' liberation seminar.
Her African National Congress Women's League said in a statement her luggage had been intercepted and broken into.

"According to her, those covert intelligence forces of the counter-revolutionary units retain the pressures on her. That ilk still remains on her and she takes strongest exception," the league reported.
Under apartheid Madikizela-Mandela was repeatedly banned, banished to a remote part of the country and detained for her defiance to white rule.
While divorced from Mandela in 1995, Madikizela-Mandela has kept her political clout through her stranglehold of the women's league top post.
